title: Quarter orbital fits remove over 99 percent of sampled signal power at 1.84416 cycles per day in KIC 3230227
abstract: We search Kepler release 25 data for extra low-frequency signals in KIC 3230227. The first three peaks match strong known modes. A fourth peak lies close to a known weak mode. A model with separate orbital terms in each quarter retains only 0.80 percent of sampled sine-wave power at 1.84416 cycles per day, but about 92 percent at the three strong frequencies. Joint fits account for this loss, but have large errors near the orbital harmonic. Four other weak peaks also have low retained power and do not establish new modes. This is a local sensitivity test, not a complete search or a detection limit. All tests use one telescope.
